summary: Reboxetine is a selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (NARI) used for major depression in countries where it is licensed (EU and others). Usual dosing is 4 mg twice daily, increased after a few weeks up to 10 mg/day, with reduced starting doses in the elderly and in renal or hepatic impairment. Common effects reflect noradrenergic activity (insomnia, dry mouth, constipation, sweating, urinary hesitancy, tachycardia). It is not FDA-approved; data derive from the EU SmPC and BNF.
indications: Acute treatment of major depressive illness / depression and maintenance of clinical improvement in patients who initially respond

dosage.d: 4 mg twice daily (8 mg/day); after 3-4 weeks may increase to 10 mg/day if needed
2 mg twice daily; may increase to 6 mg/day

dosage.n: Increase only with caution per response

admin: Take orally, usually as two divided doses
Can be taken with or without food
Take the second dose earlier in the day if insomnia occurs
Do not stop abruptly; taper to limit discontinuation symptoms
Allow several weeks to assess antidepressant response
moa: Reboxetine selectively inhibits the reuptake of noradrenaline (norepinephrine) at the presynaptic neuronal transporter, increasing noradrenergic neurotransmission. It has little effect on serotonin or dopamine reuptake and low affinity for muscarinic, histaminergic and adrenergic receptors, which underlies its antidepressant action and noradrenergic side-effect profile.

relative: Bipolar disorder (risk of switch to mania)
Severe renal or hepatic impairment (reduced dose)
Concomitant MAO inhibitors or potent CYP3A4 inhibitors
monitor: Mood, suicidal ideation (especially early and in young adults)

preg: Limited human data; avoid during pregnancy unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk. Neonates exposed in late pregnancy should be observed for discontinuation/adaptation effects.
lact: Reboxetine is excreted in breast milk; breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: Reduce the starting dose to 2 mg twice daily in significant renal impairment and titrate cautiously, as clearance is reduced.
hepatic: Reduce the starting dose to 2 mg twice daily in hepatic impairment and titrate slowly, as exposure is increased.

major: MAO inhibitors - risk of hypertensive crisis/serotonin-noradrenergic toxicity; avoid combination
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, macrolides, ritonavir, azoles) - markedly increased reboxetine levels; avoid
moderate: Other antidepressants - additive effects/serotonin syndrome risk
Diuretics / drugs causing hypokalaemia - additive electrolyte/QT concerns
minor: CYP3A4 inducers - may reduce reboxetine levels
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause hyponatraemia and modest increases in heart rate/blood pressure.

serious: Suicidal thoughts/behaviour (especially in young adults early in treatment)

monitoring: Mood and suicidal ideation, particularly during initiation and dose changes
Urinary symptoms, especially in older men
Serum sodium where hyponatraemia is suspected
counsel: It may take several weeks to feel the full benefit
Tell your doctor urgently about worsening mood or thoughts of self-harm, especially early on
Report difficulty passing urine, a fast heartbeat, or marked sleep disturbance
Do not stop suddenly - your doctor will reduce the dose gradually
Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine
pk: Store below 25 C, protected from moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved; licensed in the EU and elsewhere - data from SmPC/BNF
Selective noradrenergic action - useful when serotonergic side effects (e.g. sexual dysfunction) are a concern
Side effects reflect noradrenergic drive: insomnia, sweating, tachycardia, urinary hesitancy
Metabolised by CYP3A4 - avoid strong inhibitors and MAOIs
Taper on discontinuation to limit withdrawal symptoms
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next dose, in which case skip it and resume the schedule. Do not double the dose. To avoid insomnia, do not take a delayed dose late in the evening.
overdose: Reported overdoses caused sweating, tachycardia, changes in blood pressure and anxiety/agitation. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive care, cardiac and blood pressure monitoring.
